history.summary: CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KARNATAKA, not the value shown in the CSV. CSV town hint 'Badami' is approximate; the temple is at CHOLACHAGUDDA, about 5 km from Badami town. Major Shakti shrine in the Tilakaaranya forest, deity a form of Parvati as Shakambhari ('vegetable goddess'). The original shrine is dated to the 7th century; sources conflict on the patron - most cite the Badami Chalukya kings (who held her as tutelary deity), some cite a 603 CE installation by Jagadekamalla I (verify - the Kalyani vs Badami Chalukya attribution conflicts across sources). The present structure was renovated/rebuilt in 1750 CE by Maratha chieftain Parusharam Agale. A 1019 CE Kannada inscription on a northern pillar records Rashtrakuta king Bhimadeva. Legend (Skanda/Padma Purana) says Shakambhari emerged from a yagna to kill the demon Durgamasura. She is kuladeivam for the Devangar (weaver) community and Deshastha Brahmins. name: Banashankari Amma Temple
town_description: Cholachagudda is a small temple village about 5 km from Badami in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, set in the Tilakaaranya forest. It is known almost entirely for the Banashankari Devi temple, which draws pilgrims from Karnataka and Maharashtra, especially during the January-February jatre.
